2026-09-22.patch_summary: This patch adds a set of self-tests to exercise the MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT features in the Linux kernel. The tests cover both user-visible contracts, such as verifying that MADV_COLD does not populate PTE holes and that PAGEOUT preserves unevictable base pages, and implementation details, including testing the behavior of partial and full MADV_COLD on various types of THPs (Transparent Huge Pages). The patch also includes two additional stress tests that use implementation-specific setup to test the behavior of MADV_COLD and PAGEOUT in specific scenarios. The goal is to detect unintended changes during a planned refactor of the page-table walker.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Lorenzo expressed concern about including stress tests in selftests, citing potential issues with long run times or excessive memory usage, but noted that benchmarks like THP stress tests might be acceptable

Reviewer Lorenzo (ARM) suggested splitting the patch into smaller parts due to its large size, citing that it exercises different test areas and can be logically split across those.
sentiment_signals: questioning the inclusion of stress tests
reviews.raw_body:
I think in general we want to avoid putting stress tests as part of the
selftests in general? Or at least if they might take a long time to run or
excessive memory usage, etc.

Though that might be benchmarks, as we have the THP stress tests so maybe it's
OK?

---

In any case I really do think this should be split out into smaller parts, this
is a _gigantic_ change :)

Since you list a whole bunch of different test areas and you're exercising
different things you should be able to split this out logically across those I
think?

I like the idea of establishing some sort of invariants first before
implementing changes though in general.

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that their original patch submission was too large and promised to find a better email hosting solution, implying further revisions will be necessary.

The author is addressing Lorenzo's feedback about the patch size, specifically whether all implementation detail tests should be retained or only contractual tests. The author agrees that only contractual tests should be shipped and suggests keeping some implementation details for individual inspection.
reviews.raw_body:
Absolutely, but alas my poor email hosting throttles me if i send too
many emails - and sending a 38-part series where the important part is
the endpoint of the refactor moreso than the individual tests...
instant 24-hour timeout.

I'm working on a solution.  Need better hosting.

---

As mentioned, this was originally ~28 patches split out, but i think
ultimately only the contractual tests should be shipped.

Maybe there's an argument for keeping some of the implementation
details - they're fairly easy to find in the code below for individual
inspection.

Examples

contractual: These tests won't change behavior based on implementation
 - authorized file PAGEOUT evicts a clean file page;
 - unauthorized shared-file PAGEOUT leaves the page resident; and
 - private-file PAGEOUT reclaims a COW page but preserves a file page.

implementation detail: behavior can change without breaking a contract
 - full and partial MADV_COLD on a PTE-mapped THP

~Gregory

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lorenzo suggested splitting a large patch into smaller, more manageable self-tests, citing potential intimidation factor of large series
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks! But yeah damn indeed you do! :)

Though larger series can scare people off so maybe better to send the tests
separately?

2026-09-23.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to exercise the MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT functionality in the Linux kernel. The tests cover both user-visible contracts, such as verifying that MADV_COLD does not populate PTE holes and that PAGEOUT preserves unevictable base pages, as well as implementation details like folio and page-table behavior under various scenarios. The patch includes 28 cases to test these behaviors, with some tests intentionally asserting specific conditions to detect unintended changes during a planned refactor of the page-table walker.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) requested breaking down the large patch into smaller, reviewable pieces and removing special-case tests that are hard to maintain.
reviews.raw_body:
In any case, we have to break this down into reviewable pieces. We neglected
selftests for too long.

... and there are some schlopped tests in there that we really shouldn't have as
they are way too special and hard to maintain.

Like this monstrosity:

+/*
+ * A folio faulted on another CPU can remain in that CPU's pending LRU batch.
+ * MADV_COLD drains only the calling CPU and must safely skip the non-LRU
+ * folio without changing the mapping.
+ */
+static void test_madvise_cold_remote_lru_batch(void)
+{

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that some tests can be deleted without losing fidelity, agrees to show the work, and suggests removing ~15-20 tests.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah the intent of these particular tests was to ensure I capture ever
weird branch in the code before i went refactoring it so I ensured there
was no loss of fidelity.

I think we can reasonably delete ~15-20 of these tests.  That said, the
code itself is not schlopp, but I believe in showing the work.

~Gregory
